name: Heriot-Watt University Dubai
englishBachelors: All programmes: engineering, construction, business, computer science, psychology, design and fashion — awarding the Scottish Heriot-Watt degree.
note: A British branch campus awarding the same degree as Edinburgh, with transfers between the Dubai, Edinburgh and Malaysia campuses mid-degree. Strong in construction and engineering, which is what Dubai actually does.
summary: British campus in Dubai (opened 2005) awarding Heriot-Watt degrees, with about 30 undergraduate programmes in engineering, computing, business, psychology and design.
about: Heriot-Watt degrees are Scottish honours degrees, so many are four years and some are titled MA (Hons). You can transfer between the Dubai, Edinburgh and Malaysia campuses through Go Global.

ib.text: Each programme asks for the IB Diploma with 24 points and 3 HL plus 3 SL; Computer Science needs Maths, engineering Maths and Physics. No Course Results rule is published; ask admissions.

noDeadline: Rolling; applications accepted until 3 weeks before the start
notes: IB entry (Year 1): the IB Diploma with at least 24 points, with 3 HL and 3 SL subjects. Computer Science asks for Maths among them, Mechanical Engineering for Maths and Physics; International Business Management names no subject. The page says the course director decides after looking at individual subject scores.
IB Course Results: no rule for IB certificates or single IB subjects was found. Ask admissions whether they count for entry. Year 2 (direct) entry has its own criteria on each programme page.

Dates: Dubai admissions are rolling all year. Most students apply 6-10 months before they start; applications are accepted until 3 weeks before the intake, but a late file delays services such as your student card. Every programme has a September intake; some also start in January. No closing date is published.

Decision: the page says review normally takes 2-6 weeks from a complete file. Offers are unconditional or conditional; an unconditional offer must be accepted within 2 weeks. Starting can be deferred for up to a year.
Application fee: AED 500 plus VAT (AED 525) for each application form submitted. Scanned documents are accepted at application.

English proof: IELTS Academic 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72 (tests before 21 Jan 2026; reading 18, listening 17, speaking 19, writing 17) or 4 overall with no part below 4 (from 21 Jan 2026), PTE 50-57 with 51 in each part, or Duolingo 120. Degrees are taught and assessed in English. Whether the IB English grade can replace a test is not stated.

Tuition for September 2027 or January 2028 entry, UAE and International students, including VAT: Computer Science AED 82,264 a year; International Business Management AED 78,650 a year. Fees are reviewed each year. Mechanical Engineering's fee was not captured.

Duration: each programme page says 3-4 years and mentions a 3-year honours option. Computer Science is described as a four-year honours degree and the university calls the MA (Hons) a four-year undergraduate degree, so four years is shown for Year 1 entry.

languageOfInstruction.note: Heriot-Watt Dubai says its degrees are taught and assessed in English and sets English tests for entry.

admissionRoutes.text: The Diploma with 24 points, 3 HL and 3 SL meets Year 1 entry; Maths (and Physics for engineering) are mandatory where named.
No rule for IB certificates or single subjects was found on the programme or entry pages.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: A four-year honours degree balancing theory and practice, from software development to machine learning and data mining.
programmes.overview: In year 1 you build programming and web skills and study logic, discrete mathematics and computer systems. Later years add advanced topics such as machine learning, computational intelligence and data mining. September entry runs on Heriot-Watt semesters, with Go Global transfers to other campuses available.
programmes.ib: IB Diploma 24 points with 3 HL and 3 SL, including Maths.
programmes.selectionNote: The course director decides after reviewing relevant subject scores.
